sentences.text:
Bench: Kongara Vijaya Lakshmi
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Kongara Vijaya Lakshmi
 Criminal Petition No.6269 of 2019
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed, under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioner/accused in Cr.No.333 of 2019 on the file of Ongole Taluka PS registered for the offences under Sections 420, 272, 273,188, 328 of IPC and Sections 57, 58, 59, 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the FSS Act').
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.

Learned counsel for the petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the police are not authorised to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition No.3731 of 2018 & batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under IPC and FSS Act.

So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C., no court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such officer of the Court as that court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other court to which that court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the FIR is registered suo moto on the report of the Sub Inspector of Police, Ongole Taluka PS.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C. so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

As regards to the offence under Section 328 of IPC is concerned, the learned counsel relies on the judgment of the Bombay High Court, wherein the Court held that manufacturing and possession of gutka and Pan Masala would not amount to administering poison by any stretch of imagination.

Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner in Cr.No.333 of 2019 on the file of Ongole Taluka PS registered for the offences under Sections 420, 272, 273,188, 328 of IPC and Sections 57, 58, 59, 63 Gonugunta Rama Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 23 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46158445/
1 of the FSS Act are hereby quashed.
